title: Optimal timing of thoracic radiotherapy with osimertinib in unresectable EGFR-mutant non-small cell lung cancer

sections.title: 研究问题
sections.text:
《Optimal timing of thoracic radiotherapy with osimertinib in unresectable EGFR-mutant non-small cell lung cancer》：研究问题的原文依据。

【Abstract · abstract-1-2】The aim of the present study was to investigate the relationship between the interval from osimertinib treatment to TRT interval and the survival outcomes, defining an optimal therapeutic window for unresectable EGFR-mutant NSCLC.

evidence.text: The aim of the present study was to investigate the relationship between the interval from osimertinib treatment to TRT interval and the survival outcomes, defining an optimal therapeutic window for unresectable EGFR-mutant NSCLC.

sections.title: 研究方法
sections.text:
《Optimal timing of thoracic radiotherapy with osimertinib in unresectable EGFR-mutant non-small cell lung cancer》：方法与研究设计的原文依据。

【Abstract · abstract-1-3】Data from 175 patients with stage IIIB/IV EGFR-mutant NSCLC receiving first-line osimertinib and consolidation TRT were retrospectively analyzed.

evidence.text: Data from 175 patients with stage IIIB/IV EGFR-mutant NSCLC receiving first-line osimertinib and consolidation TRT were retrospectively analyzed.

sections.title: 主要结果
sections.text:
《Optimal timing of thoracic radiotherapy with osimertinib in unresectable EGFR-mutant non-small cell lung cancer》：结果的原文依据；数值与适用人群以引文为准。

【Abstract · abstract-1-5】At a median follow-up time of 25.3 months, each 1-day delay in the osimertinib-to-TRT interval was identified as an independent adverse prognostic factor for locoregional progression-free survival [hazard ratio (HR), 1.02; 95% confidence interval (CI), 1.01-1.02; P<0.001], progression-free survival (HR, 1.01; 95% CI, 1.01-1.02; P<0.001), and overall survival (HR, 1.02; 95% CI, 1.01-1.02; P<0.001).

【Abstract · abstract-1-6】The RCS model revealed a significant non-linear J-shaped association (non-linear P<0.05), with risk peaking between 40 and 102 days.

evidence.text: At a median follow-up time of 25.3 months, each 1-day delay in the osimertinib-to-TRT interval was identified as an independent adverse prognostic factor for locoregional progression-free survival [hazard ratio (HR), 1.02; 95% confidence interval (CI), 1.01-1.02; P<0.001], progression-free survival (HR, 1.01; 95% CI, 1.01-1.02; P<0.001), and overall survival (HR, 1.02; 95% CI, 1.01-1.02; P<0.001).
The RCS model revealed a significant non-linear J-shaped association (non-linear P<0.05), with risk peaking between 40 and 102 days.
